title: “One who avoids sensual desires As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head — That mindful one transcends This attachment in the world. Whoever is greedy…
content:
“One who avoids sensual desires
As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one transcends
This attachment in the world.

Whoever is greedy for sensual pleasures —
Land, gold, cows, horses,
Servants, attendants, women, relatives —

Weak, overcome by sensual pleasures,
Calamity crushes him,
Suffering follows him
As water rushes into a broken boat.

Therefore, always mindful,
One should abandon sensual pleasures.
Having abandoned them, one crosses the flood,
Having bailed out the boat, one reaches the far shore.”

title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
content: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of greed, monks, these six things should be developed.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise attention. Through wise attention, monks, unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to full development.”

title: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out…
content: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out any of its limbs or its neck, I will seize it right there, break it, and eat it.’ But, monks, because the tortoise did not stretch out any limb or its neck, the jackal became disenchanted with the tortoise and left, not having gained an opportunity. So too, monks, Māra constantly and relentlessly stands in ambush for you, thinking: ‘Perhaps I can gain an opportunity through the eye … through the tongue … through the mind.’ Therefore, monks, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the eye, practice restraint of the eye. When you hear a sound … smell an odor … taste a flavor … feel a touch … cognize a phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the mind, practice restraint of the mind. Monks, when you live guarding the sense faculties, Māra will become disenchanted with you and leave, not gaining an opportunity, just like the jackal with the tortoise.”

title: Elder Nun Abhayā: O fearless nun! This body is so fragile — Worldlings here, Delighting, are often lustful. I will abandon this body, Mindful and…
content:
Elder Nun Abhayā:

O fearless nun!
This body is so fragile —
Worldlings here,
Delighting, are often lustful.
I will abandon this body,
Mindful and clearly comprehending.

Without heedlessness, I will strive,
I will strive to escape the painful state.
With craving destroyed, I have attained —
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

title: “Monks, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Pleasant feeling, monks, should be seen as suffering. Painful feeling should…
content:
“Monks, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Pleasant feeling, monks, should be seen as suffering. Painful feeling should be seen as a dart. Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling should be seen as impermanent. When, monks, a monk sees pleasant feeling as suffering, sees painful feeling as a dart, sees neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as impermanent — then, monks, he is called a monk who has right view, who has cut off craving, who has destroyed the fetters. By thoroughly breaking through conceit, he has made an end of suffering.

One who sees pleasure as suffering,
And sees pain as a dart,
Sees the neutral feeling
As impermanent —
That monk sees rightly,
Fully understanding feelings.

Having fully understood feelings,
He is defilement-free in this very life.
At the breaking of the body, that Dhamma-abider,
The great sage, is beyond measure.”

title: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied, infatuated, utterly committed to these five strands of sensual pleasure, who do not see their peril, who…
content: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied, infatuated, utterly committed to these five strands of sensual pleasure, who do not see their peril, who do not know the escape from them, and who enjoy them—they should be understood as having fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and are being used by Māra as he wishes. Monks, just as a forest deer that has fallen into a trap must lie down—that deer should be understood as having fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is being used by the hunter as he wishes. When the hunter comes, the deer cannot leave as it wishes. So too, monks, those ascetics or brahmins who are tied … are being used by Māra as he wishes.”

title: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind…
content: “Monks, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, my mind becomes inflamed when they are present, and diminishes when they are future, not yet attained.’ Then, monks, I thought: ‘The five strands of sensual pleasure that this mind formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — regarding them, for my own benefit, I will dwell heedful, protecting my mind with mindfulness.’ Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — your minds become inflamed when they are present, and diminish when they are future, not yet attained. Therefore, monks, regarding the five strands of sensual pleasure that your minds formerly experienced — now past, ceased, changed — for your own benefit, dwell heedful, protecting your minds with mindfulness.”

title: Māra: You are young and beautiful, I am young and in my prime. With the five-tuned lute, Enjoy yourself, Khemā. Elder Nun Khemā: With this…
content:
Māra:

You are young and beautiful,
I am young and in my prime.
With the five-tuned lute,
Enjoy yourself, Khemā.

Elder Nun Khemā:

With this foul body,
Diseased and fragile —
I am disenchanted, disgusted.
Sensual desire has been uprooted.

Sensual desires are like swords and spears —
The aggregates are a chopping block.
What you call sensual pleasure —
I have now abandoned it.

Everywhere, delight is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know this, O Evil One —
You are defeated, Māra.

You worship the stars!
You worship fire in the deep forest —
You do not know the truth —
Fools think it is pure.

But I pay homage
To the Awakened One, the Supreme Man,
Who has escaped all suffering,
Following the Teacher’s instruction.

title: Standing to one side, the deity Candana recited this verse to the Blessed One: How can one cross the flood, Steadfast and persevering day and…
content:
Standing to one side, the deity Candana recited this verse to the Blessed One:
How can one cross the flood,
Steadfast and persevering day and night?
Without stalling, without clinging —
Who does not sink in the abyss?

(The Blessed One):
One who always has virtue,
Wisdom, and is well-concentrated,
With aroused energy and strength —
That one crosses the hard-to-cross flood.
One who has abandoned perception of lust,
Who has crossed beyond the fetter of form,
Who has destroyed delight and craving for existence —
That one does not sink in the abyss.
